D3: No audit_links provided in per-protocol context. No audit PDF fetched. GitHub repos reference ccip-owner-contracts but no audit PDF URL was discovered in the fetched pages. Recorded in unknowns.

D4: The original smartcontractkit/ccip GitHub repo is archived (Mar 14, 2025). Active onchain development moved to smartcontractkit/chainlink; offchain to smartcontractkit/chainlink-ccip. No broadcast/run-latest.json or hardhat-deploy artifacts fetched due to fetch budget; no commit SHA pinnable from this run. Recorded in unknowns.

D5: 18 chains listed in protocol.chains. Only Ethereum mainnet contracts fetched directly. Directory pages exist for Avalanche, Base, Binance, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Linea, and others but were not fetched due to fetch budget. Ethereum OnRamp addresses per-destination include lanes to Avalanche (0xaFd31C0C78785aDF53E4c185670bfd5376249d8A), Arbitrum One (0x69eCC4E2D8ea56E2d0a05bF57f4Fd6aEE7f2c284), Base (0xb8a882f3B88bd52D1Ff56A873bfDB84b70431937), and others. All other chains' Router/RMN/TokenAdminRegistry addresses are unknown.

D6: TokenAdminRegistry at 0xb22764f98dD05c789929716D677382Df22C05Cb6 is a factory-like registry with 185 tokens listed on Ethereum mainnet. Read-API enumeration (getPool, allPools) not attempted due to fetch budget. Cap notice: 185 token pools on Ethereum mainnet alone; factory enumeration deferred to next run.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: router (immutable), guardian (RMN), factory (TokenAdminRegistry), other (RegistryModuleOwner), multisig (MCMS/ManyChainMultiSig), timelock (RBACTimelock implied by upgradability docs). Timelock address not yet separately discovered — upgrade proposals pass through RBACTimelock per docs but address not found in fetched pages.

D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to fetched docs pages. MCMS address 0xE53289F32c8E690b7173aA33affE9B6B0CB0012F sourced from upgradability page with direct Etherscan link embedded. Other addresses sourced from CCIP directory page with embedded Etherscan links.

protocol_metadata.about: Chainlink CCIP (Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol) is a bridge and messaging protocol enabling token transfers and arbitrary data messages across 70+ public and private blockchains. Users can send tokens, arbitrary data, or programmable token transfers (tokens + instructions atomically) via the Router contract on each chain. CCIP uses Decentralized Oracle Networks (DONs) for cross-chain message validation, with a defense-in-depth model including an independent Risk Management Network (RMN). The Router contract is intentionally immutable; other contracts (OnRamps, OffRamps, FeeQuoter) are upgraded via redeploy-and-redirect through an RBACTimelock gated by a ManyChainMultiSig (MCMS) with node-operator veto rights.
